notes: The payload of each state is what gets JSON.serialize'd into RouterResetCardData.routerJSON. The 'default' state is what RouterResetCardDemo returns. Each metric is { label, value, state, bar } where state is ok, warn, or fault and bar is a 0-100 fill — a visual scale, not a unit, so a good reading is always a full bar. device.health drives the pill and accepts Healthy, Degraded, or Offline.

states.label: Degraded gateway
states.description: The main case: the line is clean but the gateway is losing packets on a congested channel, and it has been restarting itself for weeks. The diagnosis and the remedy are in the same card.

payload.verdict: Degraded — a restart should clear this
payload.summary: The fiber line into the home is clean and the gateway is holding a WAN session, but it is dropping 6.4% of packets and its Wi-Fi radio is sharing channel 6 with eleven neighboring networks. That combination is what the customer is experiencing as buffering and dropped calls.
payload.recommendation: Send a network-side restart. It re-provisions the WAN session and moves the Wi-Fi radio to a clear channel, which a customer power-cycle cannot do. The unit has also restarted itself 14 times in 30 days and is out of warranty, so plan on replacing it as the permanent fix.

states.label: Healthy gateway
states.description: Every reading in spec, so the card argues against the restart instead of offering it. A genuinely different rendering: no warning flag, no reboot history, and the action row drops to a follow-up. Worth showing, because a card that only ever looks alarming teaches the rep to distrust it.

payload.summary: The line into the home is clean, the gateway is holding a stable WAN session at 14 ms, and its Wi-Fi radio has channel 44 largely to itself. No packet loss in the last 24 hours.
payload.recommendation: No restart needed — it would take the customer offline for 90 seconds and change nothing. If they are still reporting slowness, the bottleneck is inside the home rather than on the gateway.

states.label: No gateway on the account
states.description: Nothing to diagnose, because the customer runs their own router. Worth designing deliberately — it is a common answer, and the useful thing to say is why the check cannot see anything rather than that it found nothing.

states.label: Error
states.description: The sentinel shape. The service returns this instead of null so the card still mounts and can say what went wrong.

payload.error: Could not reach the gateway diagnostics service. Try again in a moment.
